title: feat(plugin-auth)!: auth.handleRequest answers the plugin's whole auth surface
body:
Fixes #32637

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — a host that forwards to `AuthManager.handleRequest`, and the runtime dispatcher's `/auth` domain, now run the mount-layer checks (the IP allow-list, the one-account-per-request rule, the organization IP list and the platform-admin wrappers), so a request admitted today can be refused: for example `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED` when `allowed_ip_ranges` is set and neither a transport peer nor a trusted proxy (`server.trustProxy`) is declared.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up #32725 — content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx (its `handleRequest` section does not yet say that a forwarding host gains the whole surface and the mount-layer checks, nor name the optional transport argument); no file under `skills/**` teaches `auth.handleRequest`, `allowed_ip_ranges` or `trustProxy`.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：登录插件把现成的"挂登录路由"函数在每个内核的一张私有路由表上再调用一次，`auth.handleRequest` 改为经这张表回答插件的全部登录接口（框架自挂的 42 条加 better-auth 的全部）；自托管仍在原调用点、按原顺序挂同一批路由，接口契约形状不变。
- 为什么改：托管等宿主把登录请求转给 `handleRequest`，以前只到 better-auth，框架自挂的接口一律 404，只能在 cloud 逐条照抄；现在宿主不改代码就拿到全部接口和同样的挂载层检查（维护者裁决「同意 S1」，评审补充项全部落地）。
- 风险与回滚：托管升级钉版后开始执行挂载层检查（IP 白名单、单账号、平台管理员门），设了 `allowed_ip_ranges` 的环境行为会变，cloud#4384 负责灰度；路由内部故障的回答改为通用文案，自托管同样。回滚即回退本 PR，接口形状未变。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`（`bindAuthRouteSurface` 和 catch-all 里 `table === 'private'` 的分支）、`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`（`handleRequest` / `handleVendorRequest` / `ownsRoute`）、`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-handle-request-surface.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/auth-handle-request-surface.test.ts`，预期 62 passed，其中 42 条按路由登记表逐条派生。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`AuthPlugin` runs its auth route registration on two tables, from one function (`mountAuthRoutes`):

- **host** — the composed HTTP server's raw app, from `kernel:ready` under `registerRoutes`, exactly as before: same calls, same order, the four `basePath/*` middlewares, the catch-all and the root-path OIDC discovery documents. `registerAuthRoutes(httpServer, ctx)` keeps the `getRawApp` probe and hands the raw app to `mountAuthRoutes`.
- **private** — a Hono app built in `init()` right after the `AuthManager` exists and bound to it (`AuthManager.bindRouteSurface`) before the `auth` service is registered. It leaves out the root-path discovery documents (a host serves its own), declares that it serves no sign-in page (the mobile hand-off answers a signed-out navigation 401 and probes nothing), lets an exception reach `handleRequest`'s caller as a rejection (the catch-all rethrows and the table's `onError` rethrows), and logs no start-up line.

`AuthManager`:

- `handleRequest(request, transport)` answers a request under `basePath` through the bound table, with `transport.remoteAddress` carried in the table's env where the mount-layer checks read the peer. No bound table, or a path outside `basePath`, goes to `handleVendorRequest`.
- `handleVendorRequest` is the previous body (better-auth alone). The six internal re-dispatch callers use it: the catch-all, `handleWithTransportOf`, `admin/remove-user`, `admin/has-permission`, the sys-session revoke slice and the third-party-initiated SSO start in `runSsoCallback`.
- `ownsRoute` also answers `true` for a route the table serves itself, judged by method and path (HEAD as GET); `ownsVendorRoute` is the previous body, which the catch-all now asks.

Transport peer: `@objectstack/hono`'s embed passes the peer `@hono/node-server` reports on `c.env.incoming`; the dispatcher's `/auth` domain passes `context.request.remoteAddress` (the identity step's convention). `IAuthService.handleRequest` keeps its one-parameter shape and gains one sentence of description.

Route answers: the 30 route catches that answered `INTERNAL_ERROR` with the thrown error's message, `/config`'s `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR`, and the host catch-all now answer `Internal server error`; each logs the error (`/config` gained its log line).

`hono` moves to `dependencies` (lockfile importer entry follows). One sentence of the `one-time-token/handoff` ledger note is updated to say a forwarding host is now answered by this mount.

## Tests

New file `src/auth-handle-request-surface.test.ts` (62 cases), every composition the real `AuthPlugin.init()` with the in-memory engine and `registerRoutes: false`:

- (i) every `source: 'objectstack'` row of `AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER` (42 today, derived, so a later row is covered with no edit) answered through `handleRequest` is not better-auth's disclaiming 404; a control leg per row proves better-auth alone disclaims it.
- (ii) the private table registers the same routes in the same order as the host app, except the root discovery documents, and every one sits under the auth base; the start-up line is said once.
- Errors: a throwing vendor entry (async and synchronous) makes `handleRequest` reject; the host table answers the same fault with the generic body and logs it; `/config`'s own fault names no exception text.
- Peer: the transport reaches the vendor entry; allow-list judged by the handed peer; allow-list + `trustProxy` + `X-Forwarded-For` outside the ranges refused 403 `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `/config` exempt.
- Fallbacks: unbound manager, path outside the base and the bare base reach the vendor entry; an unknown path is better-auth's own 404, never Hono's text one; `ownsRoute` by method and path.
- Bridges with an admin session (`admin/sso/register`, `admin/remove-user`): one `handleRequest` call, inner route reached; the allow-list middleware runs once per bridged request on the self-hosted mount and through `handleRequest`.
- Hand-off: the private table answers a signed-out navigation 401 without asking anything, while the host app serving the Console answers 302.

Peer pins in the existing harness files: `packages/adapters/hono/src/hono-auth-owned-404.test.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/auth-forward-fault-sanitization.test.ts`. Existing plugin-auth stand-ins that replaced the manager's `handleRequest` / `ownsRoute` for the catch-all and the bridges now replace `handleVendorRequest` / `ownsVendorRoute` (nine files).

## Acceptance notes

- **Changeset level is `patch`, not the `minor` the card names.** `Metadata-protocol: none` (from the claim) makes every entry `patch`: AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 and the level axis of `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ("a declared `none` must grade every entry it introduces `patch`"). Raised to the seat.
- A security item is with the owner seat.
- The dispatcher fallback inside the `@objectstack/hono` embed (`dispatcher.handleAuth(path, method, body, { request: c.req.raw })`, reached only when the adapter's kernel has no `auth` service) carries no peer: `HttpProtocolContext` has no field for it, and `http-dispatcher.ts` is outside this card's surface.
- `check:auth-mount-ledger` is unchanged and green (49 mounts, 0 pending); `auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` is unchanged and green.
- Diff: 23 files, +913 / -106 (1,019 changed lines), under the 3,000-line class.
- `packages/runtime/src/auth-forward-fault-sanitization.test.ts` gained a module-top `import '@objectstack/metadata'`, which `check:test-source-alias` prescribes for an edited test that reaches that dynamic import.
